stories.label: Two Italians killed in Iranian strike on Kuwait
stories.summary: An Iranian drone attack on a Kuwaiti facility killed two Italians working for German arms maker Rheinmetall and injured four, the first reported deaths from Iranian fire since Washington and Tehran resumed exchanging strikes this month. Lead with the deaths and where they happened: a Gulf state hosting Western defence contractors is now a target, and the war's cost is landing on third countries. Note Kuwait said shrapnel came from an intercepted drone. Dateline Kuwait City.

stories.label: Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos wins race to be next ECB president
stories.summary: Former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos will succeed Christine Lagarde at the European Central Bank after the EU's biggest countries backed him. Lead with what the choice signals for the ECB rate path while inflation is back across the West: a southern-European dove or pragmatist steering the euro, and who lost the race (the Dutch candidate). Name the ECB rate and the euro as the series. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: How can the EU continue to afford supporting Ukraine?
stories.summary: EU leaders meeting in Brussels are struggling to agree the bloc's long-term budget and a new €45 billion loan to cover Ukraine's wartime deficit. Lead with the money: who borrows, who guarantees it and which member states are blocking, then the mechanism (joint borrowing against the EU budget headroom vs national contributions) and what happens to Kyiv's budget if there is no deal. Report the summit outcome, not the explainer framing. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Israel's Eisenkot reaches deal with left-wing faction as coalition talks gain steam
stories.summary: New development since our 11-25 story on his first partner: Eisenkot's Yashar signed a coalition agreement with the left-wing Democrats, taking his bloc to 48 of 120 Knesset seats, 13 short of the 61 needed to oust Netanyahu, and Trump reportedly wants to meet him if he forms a government. Lead with the new seat count and the gap, then which parties could close it (Liberman, the Arab parties) and the prediction market now pricing no second mandate after the vote at 69%, up from 48% a week ago. Dateline Tel Aviv.

stories.label: King tide West Coast flooding topped California records
stories.summary: King tides boosted by El Niño-charged Pacific storms set all-time coastal flood records in California and southern Oregon, and part of the Pacifica Pier collapsed into the sea, with more flooding possible through the week. Lead with the record and the pier, then the mechanism: an astronomical high tide stacked on storm surge and El Niño-raised sea levels, a preview of routine flooding under sea-level rise, and who pays for coastal homes and infrastructure. Filed as politics, a disaster not a study. Dateline Pacifica.

stories.label: US judge blocks Trump's FCC attempt to target Disney's ABC stations
stories.summary: A federal judge barred the FCC from putting the licences of eight Disney-owned ABC stations up for early review, finding the FCC chair took Trump's rhetoric as his 'marching orders'. Lead with that finding: a court on record that a regulator used licensing power to punish a broadcaster's coverage. Explain the mechanism (licence renewal as leverage over news content), the First Amendment ground, and whether the FCC appeals. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Congenital birth defects are on the rise in Gaza. Doctors say Israel’s genocide is to blame.
stories.summary: Doctors in Gaza report a rise in congenital birth defects and link it to exposure to bombardment and toxic residues from Israeli munitions. Lead with what the doctors are counting (cases, wards, comparison with pre-war rates) and attribute the causal claim to them; then the structural point: the siege blocks the testing and specialist care that would establish the cause and treat the newborns. Distinct from our meningitis story. Dateline Gaza City.

stories.label: Inflation in Sudan: what do the figures conceal?
stories.summary: Sudan's statistics bureau put October annual inflation at 34.88% with prices up 6.23% in a single month. Lead with the monthly figure, which annualises far above the headline, then what the official index misses: war-zone markets it cannot survey, displaced families paying for rent and medicine, and the collapse of the Sudanese pound. Credit the Radio Dabanga economist's reading. Dateline Port Sudan.

stories.label: Spain gives anti-laundering unit power to freeze crypto accounts without a judge
stories.summary: A Spanish decree lets the financial intelligence unit Sepblac freeze crypto accounts for up to five business days without a judge or a foreign request, from late January pending parliament's validation. Lead with the missing judge: an administrative freeze on private funds, and the trade-off between catching laundering fast and due process. Note what safeguards, if any, apply and how it compares with EU anti-money-laundering rules. Dateline Madrid.

stories.label: Vanke Seeks Second Extension on 1.2 Billion Yuan Bond
stories.summary: China Vanke, the state-linked developer once seen as too safe to fail, is asking bondholders for a second extension on a 1.2 billion yuan ($180 million) onshore bond, with a vote on December 8, as debt deferred earlier this year comes due again. Lead with 'second extension': deferral is becoming rollover, and Shenzhen Metro's backing is not ending it. Explain what it means for China's property slump and for homebuyers with unfinished flats. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: BTC news: A tiny payment can expose IP address behind a bitcoin wallet
stories.summary: A Bitcoin Core developer found that sending a payment worth under 35 cents to a wallet is enough to learn the IP address of the computer watching it, and several wallets built on Bitcoin Core are affected. Lead with the 35 cents, then the mechanism (how the wallet's automatic rebroadcast gives the node away) and who is exposed: dissidents, journalists and people in sanctioned or capital-controlled countries who use bitcoin for privacy. Give the workaround (disabling automatic broadcasting) and whether a fix is coming.

stories.label: KI in der Migrationsverwaltung: Automatisiert ins Risiko
stories.summary: Germany plans to have AI process asylum decisions, visa applications and residence permits, and experts warn the software is to be fed especially sensitive data with too few limits on the authorities. Lead with the scope (which decisions, which agencies, what data), then the accountability gap: who answers for an automated wrong refusal, and whether it squares with the EU AI Act's high-risk rules for migration. The people affected are asylum seekers with the least power to contest it. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: 纯电销量过半，理想汽车的生意变了
stories.summary: Battery-electric cars now make up more than half of Li Auto's sales, a reversal for the company that built its business on range-extender hybrids, and TMTPost reports its operations are recovering while its profit model still has to be rebuilt. Lead with the crossover past 50%, then the mechanism: China's EV price war and the end of the hybrid advantage, and what it means for margins. A Chinese tech-press view of the country's EV shake-out. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: 5G interference can alter high-impact weather forecasts
stories.summary: Researchers at Rutgers and in Maryland, led by Behzad Golparvar, found that radio leakage from future 5G networks could contaminate satellite weather measurements and change forecasts of high-impact storms. Lead with how much a forecast shifts, then the mechanism: 5G bands sit next to the frequencies satellites use to sense water vapour, and spectrum auctions are setting the leakage limits. Who pays: countries that rely on free satellite forecasts for storm warnings. Dateline New Brunswick, New Jersey.

stories.label: Kim Jong Un Makes Rare Show Of Nuclear Warheads After Snubbing Trump Talks
stories.summary: Kim Jong Un displayed warheads and ordered wider deployment of tactical nuclear weapons, declaring North Korea's nuclear status irreversible, days after rebuffing Trump's offer of talks. New since the 11-19 Yongbyon enrichment story: the shift from building fissile material to fielding battlefield nukes, which lowers the threshold for use on the peninsula. Lead with the doctrine change and the IAEA's reading; note the claims come via KCNA state media.

stories.label: Explosion occurs at oil facility in Thailand's Bangkok
stories.summary: An explosion and fire at an oil depot in Bangkok's eastern Phra Khanong district injured seven, four critically, and forced residents around the site to evacuate. Lead with the people living beside a fuel depot inside a city of 11 million, and ask what the authorities knew about the facility's safety and why homes sit so close to it.

stories.label: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen in Islamabad meeting, Khawaja Asif says
stories.summary: The Makkah mutual-defence pact meets in Islamabad today with the Saudi–Houthi war on the agenda, Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif says. The new development after the Houthi strikes on Ras Tanura and the advance on Aden: whether a pact that binds Pakistan to Saudi defence turns into a commitment of Pakistani forces. Lead with what Pakistan has promised Riyadh and what it would cost Islamabad, which is also mediating with Iran.

stories.label: OPEC+ to discuss status of production capacities assessment -- Novak
stories.summary: OPEC+ is leaning toward rolling current output quotas into January at Sunday's online meeting, delegates say, because the Iran war and mined tankers in Hormuz make 2027 targets impossible to set. New since the 11-24 Iraq capacity-review story: the rollover option itself, and Novak saying the capacity assessment will be on the table. Lead with how a cartel sets quotas when part of its members' oil cannot reach the sea; name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Elon Musk pledges to give two SpaceX shares to every child in the US
stories.summary: SpaceX will put one share into every active Trump Account, and Musk will match it from his own stake. Lead with the mechanism: a private company still seeking federal contracts and FCC approvals (the million-satellite licence) seeding a government-branded savings scheme, and what two shares are worth per child against the cost to SpaceX. Who benefits from turning tens of millions of children into SpaceX shareholders before a listing.

stories.label: Govt to limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit
stories.summary: Pakistan's government will cap the extra fuel-cost charge on December electricity bills at 83 paise per kWh, against the Rs2.88 the power sector sought, and spread the rest through quarterly forward adjustments. Lead with what households save now and who carries the deferred cost — the circular debt, the IMF programme, and fuel bills driven up by the Iran war.

stories.label: Chatkontrolle-Verhandlungen: EU-Rat will für mehr Überwachung offenbar tricksen
stories.summary: In the final round of the EU chat-control talks, the Irish Council presidency is reportedly weighing a manoeuvre to bypass the European Parliament's negotiating team, which insists scanning be targeted and need a judge's approval. Lead with the procedural trick and what it would mean for encrypted messaging of 450 million people: untargeted scanning without judicial sign-off.

stories.label: 信邦智能拟斥28.56亿“蛇吞象”，英迪芯微第一大股东退出套现9.61亿
stories.summary: Small listed automation firm Xinbang Intelligent plans a 2.856 billion yuan takeover of automotive-chip designer Indiemicro — a 'snake swallowing an elephant' deal — while Indiemicro's largest shareholder cashes out 961 million yuan. Lead with the structure: how China's domestic auto-chip makers, blocked from easy IPOs, reach public markets through backdoor acquisitions, and who exits rich.

stories.label: Thales Alenia Space to Establish Dedicated Company for Cargo Return Services
stories.summary: Thales Alenia Space will spin out a dedicated company to build and sell its space-station cargo return service, Italian unions FIM, FIOM and UILM disclosed after meeting management. Lead with why it matters: Europe has no way to bring cargo back from orbit and relies on SpaceX's Dragon, and a spin-out signals Thales wants outside capital rather than ESA money alone.

stories.label: Scientists discover quasar formed within a mere 630 million years of the Big Bang, setting a record
stories.summary: Astronomers found the most distant quasar yet, shining 630 million years after the Big Bang, powered by a black hole that is feeding slowly. Lead with the puzzle: a slow-eating black hole should not have grown that massive so early, which strengthens the case for heavy 'seed' black holes at the dawn of the universe.

stories.label: Spain activates national contingency plan
stories.summary: A cargo ship carrying more than a million litres of diesel sank off Ibiza: one sailor dead, six in hospital, and Spain has triggered its national maritime pollution contingency plan. Lead with the fuel load and the slick threat to the Balearic coast and fisheries, then the crew (who they were, what flag the ship flew, who owned and insured it) and what the contingency plan obliges the state to do. A disaster, filed as politics. Dateline Ibiza.

stories.label: Gunmen open fire at Peter Obi's rally in Edo
stories.summary: Three gunmen in a black Toyota Hilux opened fire on a rally for Peter Obi, the NDC's presidential candidate, in Benin City; police say they are hunting the attackers. Lead with what happened at the rally (casualties, who was hit) and who the police say is responsible, then the pattern: political violence against opposition campaigns ahead of Nigeria's election, and whether anyone is ever charged. Dateline Benin City.

stories.label: Iran tightens grip over Hormuz as diplomacy inches forward
stories.summary: New development in the Hormuz arc: US envoy Jared Kushner confirmed meetings with Iranian officials under a channel run by Vice President Vance, while saying Trump keeps 'all options on the table'. Lead with the talks — who is meeting, where, and on what terms — set against Iran's tightening control of the strait and the Houthi attacks. Tie it to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and to Brent crude, which climbed back above $96 this morning. Do not re-run the mine-strike or tugboat stories from 11-25. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: UniCredit to propose Andrea Orcel as chair of Commerzbank
stories.summary: New development after the EU cleared the takeover on 11-16: with final approval in hand, UniCredit has asked Commerzbank to call an extraordinary shareholder meeting and will propose its own CEO, Andrea Orcel, as chair of its German rival's supervisory board. Lead with the boardroom move — an acquirer installing its chief executive atop the target — and Berlin's long resistance, then what Europe's first big cross-border bank merger in years means for banking union. Dateline Frankfurt.

stories.label: Norse Suspends Flights, in Talks to Avoid Bankruptcy Filing
stories.summary: Norse Atlantic Airways grounded every flight on Thursday and says it will file for bankruptcy unless investors deliver short-term financing or a takeover. Lead with the stranded passengers and crew, then the mechanism: a low-cost long-haul model built on leased Boeing 787s, squeezed by jet fuel prices that the Gulf war has pushed up. Dateline Oslo.

stories.label: Tata Trusts launch first legal salvo in boardroom battle
stories.summary: The charitable trusts that control Tata Sons, India's largest conglomerate, have gone to court against N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chair: the first legal move in a feud between the Noel Tata-led trusts and the group's management. Lead with the court filing, then the structure: charities owning two-thirds of a holding company whose businesses run from steel to software, and who actually controls it. Dateline Mumbai.

stories.label: O lado oculto da Black Friday
stories.summary: Agência Pública reports on the thousands of temporary workers in Brazil who sort and deliver Black Friday orders on exhausting shifts. Lead with the most concrete finding — hours, pay, or a named warehouse or platform — then the mechanism: e-commerce peaks met with short-term contracts that carry fewer protections. Who profits, and who carries the cost. Dateline São Paulo unless the reporting places it elsewhere.

stories.label: ZEC news: Zcash developers want users to move $300 million out of an older privacy system
stories.summary: Two of Zcash's main developers are urging users to move about $300 million of ZEC out of the older Sapling shielded pool before advances in mathematics make it breakable; no working attack has been shown, and the newer Ironwood pool doesn't use the technique at issue. Lead with the pre-emptive migration — a cryptocurrency asking its users to evacuate before an attack exists — and explain which mathematical advance and which cryptographic assumption are at stake.

stories.label: SHEIN agrees to $100 million settlement over US shipping, reviews and customer-service claims
stories.summary: SHEIN will pay $100 million in consumer redress to settle FTC allegations that it broke shipping promises, suppressed negative reviews, gave inadequate customer service and made misleading supply-chain claims; a federal judge must approve it. Lead with the suppressed reviews — the platform manipulating the signal shoppers rely on — and the supply-chain claims, given scrutiny of forced labour in its cotton. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Tencent brings Hy4 flash to desktop computers with quantized model release
stories.summary: Tencent published GGUF quantized weights for its Hy4 flash model through its AngelSlim compression project, so it runs locally on a 64GB Mac mini as well as on Nvidia hardware. Lead with the smallest version's size and the hardware it needs, then the strategy: Chinese labs competing by putting open weights on consumer machines, while US labs keep frontier models behind APIs. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: Some miniature Cas12m proteins can cut DNA after all
stories.summary: A University of Tokyo team led by Osamu Nureki shows for the first time that some Cas12m proteins, among the smallest CRISPR enzymes and thought only to bind DNA, have an active state that cuts it, and maps the structural difference between the active and inactive forms. Why it matters: smaller editors fit inside the viral vectors used to deliver gene therapies. Lead with the reversal of the 'cannot cut' assumption. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: Brazil blasts 'unacceptable' new US tariff proposals
stories.summary: The US trade representative proposed new tariffs on Brazilian aircraft (a 10% duty that lands on Embraer) and sugar; Lula's office calls them unacceptable, says Brazil will not yield to threats but wants a negotiated deal and is not ruling out reciprocity. Datelined Brasília: lead with who pays — Embraer's US sales and Brazilian cane growers — and the mechanism, a Section 301-style proposal rather than an enacted duty, and what Brazil can retaliate with.

stories.label: Sharp drop in gold prices! A first in 14 months.
stories.summary: Gold plunged to its lowest in more than a year (spot near $3,580/oz, briefly lower) because hot US inflation data made Federal Reserve rate hikes likely — the opposite of the textbook 'inflation hedge' story, and Mint asks exactly why investors are dumping bullion despite inflation. Name the series: gold, and the US 10-year Treasury yield. The mechanism to teach: higher real yields raise the cost of holding a metal that pays nothing. Who it lands on: Indian and Turkish households and central banks that hold savings in gold (mint, Haberler sources).

stories.label: Rupee Hits 8-Month High as November Stock Inflows Near $15 Billion
stories.summary: Foreign investors poured nearly $15 billion into Indian stocks in November, lifting the rupee to an eight-month high (about 92.2 per dollar) while gold sank and the Fed turns hawkish. Lead with the size of the inflow and the contrast: capital fleeing to India even as US rates rise. Datelined Mumbai; note the oil-price risk Reuters flags, since India imports most of its crude and the Iran war has kept Brent high.

stories.label: Inside Nigeria-US Health Deal: What America gets in return for $2.1bn
stories.summary: Premium Times reviewed the signed Nigeria–US health cooperation agreement: in return for $2.1bn, Nigeria must share biological specimens and related data with the United States, raise domestic health spending and grant monitoring access, and a separate health-data-sharing arrangement remains unexplained. Lead with what Nigeria gives up — pathogen samples and genomic data — and the sovereignty question: who owns the specimens and any medicines developed from them. Datelined Abuja.

stories.label: Court of Appeal overturns Omokore's acquittal, convicts him in $823m oil fraud case
stories.summary: Nigeria's Court of Appeal in Abuja reversed the acquittal of oil businessman Olajide Omokore and two Atlantic Energy companies, convicting them over the diversion of about $823 million of crude oil. Lead with the reversal: a rare appellate conviction in one of the oil-sector cases tied to the Diezani Alison-Madueke era, brought by the EFCC. Explain the mechanism (strategic alliance contracts with the state oil company whose proceeds never reached the treasury) and what comes next — sentencing, asset recovery, a Supreme Court appeal.

stories.label: Ukraine attacks Russian military base, says five planes struck
stories.summary: New development in the arc where Putin vowed retaliation for Ukraine's refinery strikes: Ukraine's General Staff says it hit the Savasleyka airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region, east of Moscow, damaging five aircraft (MiG-31s and Su-34s) used to launch missiles and glide bombs. Attribute the damage claim to Kyiv. Lead with the reach — a base deep inside Russia — and the stakes for the fragile energy ceasefire.

stories.label: En el 25N, feministas exigen búsqueda inmediata ante 219 denuncias por desaparición de mujeres y niñas en lo que va de 2026
stories.summary: Honduran police investigators received 219 reports of missing women and girls from January to November 2026, and UNAH's violence observatory counted 211 violent deaths of women in January–September. Lead with the two numbers and the accountability gap: the state's search mechanisms and femicide prosecutions are failing, and on 25 November women's groups demanded funded searches and an end to impunity. Datelined Tegucigalpa.

stories.label: ESA Releases First Images from the "Hera" Asteroid Defense Mission
stories.summary: ESA's Hera probe sent the first close images of Dimorphos, four years after NASA's DART spacecraft rammed it: a stadium-sized crater and a moonlet knocked reeling. Lead with what the pictures measure — how much a kinetic impact actually reshaped and deflected the body — because that number decides whether ramming is a workable planetary defence. Include Dawn's coverage.

stories.label: 1Password Security Incident
stories.summary: 1Password published an update on a November 2026 security incident (1,280 points on Hacker News). Lead with exactly what was accessed and whether vault data or secret keys were exposed, then the mechanism of the breach and what users must do. The stakes: a password manager is a single point of failure for millions of people and businesses, and it lands in the same week as Microsoft's outage and the CIA/ODNI breaches. Datelined Toronto.

stories.label: Holy shit holy shit holy shit holy shit: The magnitude of what’s now happening
stories.summary: Quantum-computing theorist Scott Aaronson, usually the field's chief deflater of hype, posted an alarmed reaction to a new result (1,155 points, 985 comments on Hacker News). Report the underlying result he is reacting to — what was demonstrated, by whom, and with what numbers — not the blog post itself, and use Aaronson as the expert who judges its magnitude. If it concerns cryptography-breaking quantum capability or AI, lead with what it means for systems readers depend on.

stories.label: China's CATL faces a trillion-yuan question: how to win back investor confidence
stories.summary: CATL, the world's largest EV and grid-storage battery maker, has lost a large share of its market value after a reported production cut and weak battery demand, and analysts expect the pressure to last into next year. Lead with the production cut and what it says about EV and energy-storage demand — a slowdown at CATL ripples to lithium miners and to every carmaker that buys its cells. Datelined Ningde; skip the stock-tip framing and focus on what moved it.

stories.label: Multiple fatalities reported in fuel tanker fire in Egypt's Giza
stories.summary: At least 30 killed and 15 injured when a fuel tanker caught fire on Cairo's Ring Road in the Al-Warraq area of Giza, per the health ministry's preliminary count. Lead with the toll, then the accountability question: Egypt's road-safety record, hazardous-fuel trucking through dense informal districts like Al-Warraq, and who regulates it. Dateline Giza.

stories.label: Who is Chen Jining, China's latest Politburo member under investigation?
stories.summary: The CCP placed Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining, a sitting Politburo member, under investigation, while widening the anti-graft net to retired officials and to cases involving cryptocurrency or cross-border relocation. Lead with the rank: a party chief of China's financial capital. Then the mechanism: how the new targeting of crypto and flight abroad extends discipline-inspection reach. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: Netanyahu says corruption trial 'must end' as court suggests dropping case
stories.summary: New development: the judges in Netanyahu's trial recommended prosecutors drop one bribery case, and the caretaker PM now demands the whole trial end, heading into a fifth election. Lead with which case the judges flagged and why, then what remains (the other charges), and what it means for accountability of a sitting leader. Distinct from the Eisenkot coalition story already covered. Dateline Jerusalem.

stories.label: US grants SpaceX approval for 1 million space data centres
stories.summary: The FCC authorised SpaceX to launch up to 1 million satellites for orbital AI data centres. Lead with the number against today's roughly 10,000-plus active satellites in orbit. The structural point: one US regulator's licence claims orbital space and spectrum every other nation shares, with debris, astronomy and sovereignty costs borne globally. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Argentina's economy appears to enter recession as job concerns grow
stories.summary: INDEC's EMAE activity data show a second straight quarter of contraction, a technical recession under Milei, with manufacturing, retail and construction down and consumer spending falling. Lead with the sectors and job losses, then the mechanism: austerity and a strong peso squeezing domestic demand while mining and energy grow. Who pays: wage earners and small industry. Dateline Buenos Aires.

stories.label: After Pentagon Official Took Office, His Family Firm's Clients Won Up to $3.5 Billion in Military Contracts
stories.summary: Michael Dodd, assistant secretary for critical technologies at the War Department, and his family own a defense consulting firm whose clients have won up to $3.5 billion in contracts since he took office. Lead with the figure, then the mechanism: how ethics rules and recusal are supposed to work, and whether they did, while the Iran war drives procurement. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Meningitis cases surge in Gaza as deteriorating living conditions put children at risk
stories.summary: Meningitis cases in Gaza rose more than eightfold in October, driven by overcrowded displacement camps, contaminated water and collapsed sanitation under the ceasefire. Lead with the eightfold rise and the children at risk; the mechanism is the blockade on sanitation materials and medicine, continuation of the siege as the development. Dateline Gaza City or Khan Younis per the source.

stories.label: KP's Karak reports 'first polio case in 6 years', taking countrywide 2026 tally to 10
stories.summary: A 14-month-old in Karak, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is Pakistan's 10th paralytic polio case of 2026 and the district's first in six years. Lead with the child and the six-year gap, then why the virus is returning to cleared districts: missed vaccination rounds, insecurity in KP, and Pakistan's place as one of the last two endemic countries. Dateline Karak.

stories.label: 'Para onde eu vou?' Brasil é julgado na Corte Interamericana por direito de mulher trans
stories.summary: Brazil is answering before the Inter-American Court of Human Rights in the case of Luiza Melinho, the court's first ruling on the right to health of trans people, over care the Brazilian state denied her. Lead with the precedent: a ruling binds the states that accept the court's jurisdiction across Latin America. Then the case history and what the state argued. Dateline San José (the court's seat) or per the source.

stories.label: ASML's CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
stories.summary: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet, head of the sole maker of the lithography machines needed for the most advanced AI chips, argues export controls should protect the leading edge but not cut China off entirely, warning that full decoupling backfires. ASML shares are down about 10% in a week amid the AI chip sell-off; give the reader how much of ASML's revenue comes from China and what Washington and The Hague currently restrict. Dateline Veldhoven.

stories.label: The Brazilian social movement working with China to help family farms
stories.summary: Brazil's Landless Rural Workers' Movement (MST) is partnering with Chinese manufacturers to bring cheap small tractors to family farms, against resistance from the incumbent machinery makers. Lead with the price gap smallholders face, then the mechanism: a South-South supply chain bypassing the agribusiness equipment oligopoly. Dateline per source (Brasília or the MST site).

stories.label: 被红果改写的Q3财报季
stories.summary: TMTPost's read of China's Q3 earnings season: ByteDance's free short-drama app Hongguo has reshaped results for second-tier internet firms, which are cutting costs and betting on AI to survive. Lead with the firms named and the figures the piece gives for revenue or user losses, then the mechanism: a free, ad-funded app draining paid content and attention. A Chinese tech-press view of its own market. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Microsoft: China's Salt Typhoon hackers are using Artex
stories.summary: New development on the Artex AI hacking tool covered on 11-23: Microsoft now says state groups from China (Salt Typhoon, the telecom intruders) and North Korea are rapidly integrating it into their toolkits. Lead with the attribution, then the mechanism: a leaked AI tool lowering the cost of intrusion for state actors. Dateline Redmond.

stories.label: The Birds Are Listening: Scientists Used Seabirds to Track Hidden Ships
stories.summary: Researchers fitted seabirds with audio recorders and found a surprising share of vessels at sea had switched off their AIS location trackers. Lead with that share, then the mechanism: dark vessels evade fisheries enforcement and sanctions, and birds offer a cheap sensor network over oceans that patrols cannot cover. Name the study, journal and region.

stories.label: Draining peatlands leaves a long legacy of warming
stories.summary: A new study finds that drained peatlands keep warming the planet long after drainage, flipping ecosystems that removed hundreds of gigatons of CO2 into sources. Lead with the duration of the legacy effect, then where it bites: Indonesia's and Malaysia's drained tropical peat for palm oil, and northern bogs. Name the study and journal.

stories.label: Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery in retaliation for deadly strikes
stories.summary: New development beyond our Hodeidah and Riyadh-tower coverage: the Houthis now claim a strike on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and its main Gulf export terminal, framed as retaliation for Saudi strikes that killed scores of Yemeni civilians. Report the Houthi claim as a claim and give Saudi confirmation or damage as of the latest source; lead with what Ras Tanura handles and name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. Name the civilians killed in the Saudi strikes too: the war's cost runs both ways. Dateline Ras Tanura.

stories.label: Israel's Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government
stories.summary: A different story from our chemical-weapons item: Gadi Eisenkot has his first coalition partner, but both negotiation tracks are stalling and Israel is edging toward a fifth election in four years. Explain the arithmetic: who holds the seats, what the deadline is and what happens when it passes. Note that a caretaker government running wars on several fronts keeps governing while no one can form a majority. Dateline Jerusalem.

stories.label: Poundland collapses into administration
stories.summary: Poundland, one of Britain's biggest discount chains, has gone into administration with about 12,000 jobs at risk, weeks before Christmas, after its US private-equity owner Gordon Brothers could not find a buyer. Lead with the jobs and who shops there: a pound-store collapsing during a cost-of-living squeeze, with the energy price cap up 26% on the Iran war. Explain the mechanism: what a private-equity owner gains and loses in administration, and who ranks last (staff, suppliers). Dateline London.

stories.label: BYD in Exclusive Talks to Buy INEOS Factory in France
stories.summary: BYD is in exclusive talks to buy INEOS Automotive's Hambach plant in France, the former Smart factory. It would be BYD's first passenger-car plant in Western Europe. The mechanism: EU countervailing duties on Chinese EVs make it cheaper to build inside the bloc than to export to it, so tariffs are pulling Chinese capital into French industry. Give the Chinese business-press view of why, and what it means for the plant's workers. Dateline Hambach.

stories.label: Domestic violence cases in Germany hit new high
stories.summary: On the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, Germany's federal figures show recorded domestic violence at a new high. Lead with the German number and the femicide count. The cluster also carries Kerala's new scheme against domestic cyber-violence, a Dawn report from Pakistan and Mattarella's message in Italy; use them as a short comparison of what states are actually doing, not as filler. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: NDLEA busts ₦303.9bn meth lab in Enugu, arrests five Mexican meth specialists
stories.summary: Nigeria's drug agency dismantled another industrial-scale methamphetamine lab in Enugu: 1,512 kg seized, worth ₦303.9bn, and five Mexican 'cooks' arrested alongside a 63-year-old local baron. The structural story is Mexican cartel expertise moving into West Africa as a production base, not only a transit route. Lead with the Mexican cooks and say how many such labs the NDLEA has found. Dateline Enugu.

stories.label: Os rastros de Peter Thiel na Argentina
stories.summary: Agência Pública maps the network of Argentine politicians, businessmen and economic interests that drew Palantir's co-founder Peter Thiel to move to Argentina. Lead with the most concrete link the investigation documents, whether a contract, a deal or an official, and what Thiel stands to gain under Milei: data contracts, deregulation, mining or tax. This is an accountability story about a surveillance-tech billionaire buying access to a state. Dateline Buenos Aires.

stories.label: Media reaction: Who is to blame for COP31 ‘failure’?
stories.summary: We have not covered COP31's collapse in Antalya: a coalition of nations rejected the proposed 'Antalya pact' and the talks ended without a deal. Use Carbon Brief's roundup to report the event itself: which countries blocked the pact and why, what was on the table (finance, a fossil-fuel phase-out), and who blames whom. The cost falls on climate-vulnerable states. Filed as politics because this is diplomacy, not a finding. Dateline Antalya.

stories.label: AJK Assembly sets conditions for resumption of dialogue with proscribed JAAC
stories.summary: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly offered to reopen talks with the Joint Awami Action Committee, the rights movement Islamabad has banned, but only if the committee disbands armed groups, hands over people accused of serious crimes and makes an unequivocal commitment. Explain what the JAAC is: a movement that grew out of protests over electricity prices and flour subsidies. Explain why it was proscribed and what an assembly vote can and cannot change. Dateline Muzaffarabad.

stories.label: Microsoft declares 'Code Red' following 24-hour outage: Here's what that means
stories.summary: Microsoft has declared an internal 'Code Red' and made reliability its top priority after a 24-hour outage earlier this month. Lead with what failed and who went dark: Outlook, Microsoft 365, businesses and governments. The structural point is concentration risk: a single vendor's bad day halts a large share of the world's office work. Say what 'Code Red' actually changes, such as feature freezes and reassigned engineers. Dateline Redmond.

stories.label: Ladybird's new alpha shows there's life beyond Chromium
stories.summary: After four years of writing a browser engine from scratch, Ladybird has shipped its first downloadable alpha for macOS and Linux. It is the first new independent engine in years, in a market where Google's Chromium, plus Apple's WebKit and Mozilla's Gecko, decide how the web is rendered. Lead with the monoculture and why it matters for web standards and for antitrust, then what the alpha can and cannot do yet.

stories.label: Haushalt: Baden-Württemberg will massiv beim Datenschutz kürzen
stories.summary: Baden-Württemberg's budget would cut its data-protection authority's posts by 40%. The state commissioner, Tobias Keber, says that breaches the EU requirement that regulators be adequately resourced and 'takes a chainsaw to the right to complain'. The mechanism: GDPR is enforced by regional authorities, so starving one guts enforcement in Germany's industrial heartland without changing a word of the law. Dateline Stuttgart.

stories.label: Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash
stories.summary: Etsy's new terms appeared to let it train AI on sellers' artwork. After a backlash, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal has 'clarified' them, and a veteran illustrator calls the revision sugar-coating. Lead with what the terms still permit after the clarification, clause by clause, and who holds the power: small artisans who cannot leave the marketplace that brings them buyers. Part of a pattern of platforms rewriting terms to claim training rights. Dateline Brooklyn.

stories.label: New quantum network entangles 123 qubits that store information in atoms' positions
stories.summary: A study in Physical Review Letters entangles 123 atomic qubits that store information in the atoms' positions, building a platform for measurement-based quantum computing. That approach has been held back by how hard it is to address one atom or one group at a time. Lead with the 123 and what is new about encoding in position, then say plainly how far this remains from a useful quantum computer. Name the institution and dateline its city.
